Dubai mechanic leaves BMW unlocked with keys inside, woman's experience sparks online reactions
sum: A Dubai resident's unusual experience of collecting her luxury car from a garage has sparked conversations online about the city's sense of safety, after her mechanic left a BMW unlocked with its keys inside while she was away.

In a post on X, a user named Shradda shared how her car mechanic called to inform her that the vehicle was ready for collection following repairs. However, she told him that she could only visit the garage between 1.15 pm and 2.15 pm because of her work meetings.
The timing presented a small challenge. The garage was scheduled to remain closed in the afternoon for Friday prayers, but Shradda needed the car for a trip planned for the following day.

Rather than asking her to reschedule, the mechanic came up with an unexpected solution. He offered to park the BMW outside the garage and leave the keys inside the unlocked vehicle for her to collect later.

What surprised Shradda was how casually the arrangement was made. Despite the car being a BMW and left unattended with its keys inside, neither she nor the mechanic appeared particularly concerned about the possibility of theft.
She subsequently arrived during the agreed time window, collected the vehicle and drove home.

Sharing the experience, Shradda described it as another example of the sense of security she associates with living in Dubai. Her post has since drawn reactions from other residents and people who have lived in the UAE, with several sharing similar experiences.

Volkswagen drags rivals Mercedes, BMW into $1.2 billion tax fight
sum: Volkswagen is currently contesting a tax demand of $1.2 billion from Indian authorities regarding its import practices. The company claims it has been unfairly singled out, as competitors also import car parts at lower tariffs. Volkswagen argues that its rivals are using a similar parts/components model for imports and duty payments. The ongoing legal battle may have significant implications for other car manufacturers in India.
Also read: Mercedes-Benz plans new China JV for local auto part supplies

Volkswagen has denied the allegations, describing the case as a matter of "life and death" that could "wipe out" all of its investments in India, where it has just a 2% market share. The dispute coincides with the German carmaker's challenges back home due to worker disputes over pay, and falling sales in its key Chinese market.

After India accused VW of being the only carmaker indulging in such practices, the German company's unit in a non-public Mumbai court filing dated November 10 said "every manufacturer of comparable cars" follows the same "parts/components model" and pays duty at 10%.
If VW succeeds with its arguments about how its rivals import car parts, other carmakers could potentially face heightened scrutiny in the world's third-largest auto market.

"The contention that all other manufacturers paid duty at 30% while the petitioner alone paid 10% is unfortunate and factually incorrect," Volkswagen's India unit said in the filing, seen by Reuters, and being reported for the first time.
The tax demand "deserves to be quashed for requiring the petitioner alone to pay 30% duty while all other manufacturers pay 10%," it added.

BMW Shares Rebound 5.4% as JPMorgan and Kepler Cheuvreux Split on China Recovery
sum: BMW stock climbed 5.4% on Wednesday, riding a broader recovery in European auto equities that followed the sector's slide to a six-year low. The rebound came as two major brokerages staked out sharply different positions on the Munich carmaker's prospects.

At the heart of the disagreement is China. JPMorgan expects BMW's sales volumes there to stabilize, while Kepler Cheuvreux counts weak Chinese demand among the reasons it cut its price target. The divide extends well beyond that single market question.

JPMorgan reaffirmed its "Overweight" rating and 68-euro price target on Tuesday, singling out BMW in its 2027 sector outlook as an attractive dividend play. Analyst Jose Asumendi's call on China refers to unit volumes holding steady, not a return to sales growth.

That dividend framing comes with an important qualifier. For 2025, the payout stood at 4.40 euros per share. Analysts project 2.48 euros per share for 2026 — an estimate, not a distribution approved by BMW's management.

Kepler Cheuvreux, for its part, lowered its target from 56 to 53 euros on Tuesday and kept its "Reduce" recommendation. The brokerage cited upcoming model changes, soft demand in China and restructuring costs as the drags on the stock.

The gap between the two views runs deeper than their read on China. Even if volumes there steady as JPMorgan anticipates, Kepler's other two concerns — the model cycle and restructuring expenses — would remain unaddressed.

Recent quarterly figures offer a yardstick for that debate. BMW reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of 30.45 billion euros on November 4, down from 32.31 billion euros a year earlier. Earnings per share also came in below the prior-year quarter.

items.t: BMW iX4 Design Patent Filed In India
sum: The iX4 is expected to arrive on our shores via CBU (completely-built unit) route

The BMW iX4 made its global debut in October 2026, and the German marque has now filed a design patent for the model in India, hinting at a possible launch in the country in 2027. The iX4 is essentially an SUV-coupe version of the BMW iX3.

Design patent filed in India clearly reveals the iX4's design and silhouette, which appear identical to those of the international-spec model. It features a coupe roofline to distinguish itself from the regular iX3 SUV. However, it still shares a lot of design cues with its standard counterpart, including grille and headlights. Although the patent offers no clues about the alloy wheel design of the India-spec iX4, the international-spec version gets 20-inch alloy wheels.

The design patent does not reveal the iX4's cabin. However, it is expected to be largely identical to that of its global iteration, which shares its interior with the BMW iX3. It gets a 17.9-inch centre infotainment display, along with a large panoramic display that spans across the width of the dashboard. Just like other BMW Neue Klasse models, the iX4 also gets a futuristic looking 4-spoke steering wheel.

The BMW iX4 is the third Neue Klasse model from the German carmaker after the BMW iX3 and i3. It is based on BMW's 800-volt architecture paired with the automaker's 6th-generation (Gen6) eDrive technology. The global-spec iX4 comes in three powertrain configurations: 40 xDrive, 50 xDrive, and M60 xDrive.

The 40 xDrive and 50 xDrive are equipped with 82.5 kWh and 108.7 kWh battery packs, respectively. The former offers a claimed range of up to 638 km, while latter has a claimed range of up to 828 km. There's also a more powerful M60 xDrive version of the iX4, which makes 612 PS and can accelerate from 0 to 100 kmph in just 3.9 seconds. It has a claimed range of up to 777 km. It remains to be seen which of these powertrain options will make its way to India.

BMW Shares Slip as Leipzig Walkout Adds to a Week of Broker Downgrades
sum: BMW's Leipzig plant became the latest flashpoint in Germany's metalworkers' dispute on Thursday, with IG Metall reporting that several thousand employees downed tools across the early and late shifts and halted production for hours at a time. The stock responded by falling 1.3% on the day.

The Leipzig stoppage follows 24-hour walkouts on 20 November at BMW's Munich headquarters plant and its Dingolfing and Landshut sites, according to Handelsblatt — part of IG Metall's rolling programme of full-day stoppages across the metal and electrical industry. A day-long warning strike also hit the Berlin-Spandau facility, the Süddeutsche Zeitung reported, and the union has signalled further action for Friday.

Analyst sentiment has been shifting in parallel. Kepler Cheuvreux cut its BMW price target to 53 euros from 56 on Thursday while keeping a "Reduce" rating, a call that landed as the shares added 0.8% to close at 53.42 euros. RBC Capital Markets had moved a day earlier, trimming its target to 56 euros from 58 and reiterating "Sector Perform."

Tom Narayan of RBC tied the revision to takeaways from the reporting season, pointing to a sharp drop in Chinese passenger-car sales during the first half of November as a drag on the sector. The downgrades sit against a backdrop of muted expectations: on 4 November BMW lowered its guidance for the 2026 financial year, projecting an automotive EBIT margin of between minus 0.5% and plus 0.5%.

Away from the labour and ratings news, the company's share repurchase programme is running on schedule. BMW disclosed on 18 November that it had bought roughly 385,000 ordinary shares between 16 and 17 November.

There was also an expansion on the energy side. BMW and E.ON widened their offer for feeding electricity back into the grid to cover the i3, iX4 and iX5 models, with a bonus of up to 720 euros a year for participating drivers.

In the United States, BMW of North America issued a recall on 13 November covering about 721,000 vehicles because of a fire risk. A connector on the water pump can cause a short circuit, and the NHTSA advised owners to park the affected cars outdoors until repairs are completed.

items.t: BMW Readies 2027 R 1300 R at $16,695
sum: BMW's flagship boxer-powered roadster carries over into the 2027 model year with an added touring package.

BMW's 2027 R 1300 R roadster will launch with a starting price of $16,695, unchanged from the previous model year. The motorcycle carries over from the 2026 redesign without significant mechanical changes and adds a new touring package.

The unchanged starting price keeps the flagship boxer-powered roadster accessible within BMW's lineup as buyers weigh it against the R 1300 RS and R 1300 GS. The added touring package expands the bike's practicality for riders who want luggage and longer-distance use.

The 1,300cc air/liquid-cooled boxer twin produces 145 horsepower at 7,750 rpm and 110 lb-ft of torque at 6,500 rpm, with a curb weight of 527 pounds and a 30.9-inch seat height. Front suspension offers 5.5 inches of travel, while the rear offers 5.1 inches.
BMW is a German automaker and motorcycle manufacturer known for its boxer-engine motorcycles, including the R 1300 series.

The R 1300 R uses a 47mm inverted telescopic fork, dual 310mm front discs, and a 285mm rear disc with fully integrated cornering ABS. A 6.5-inch TFT display offers smartphone connectivity, and the 2027 touring package adds left and right luggage-case holders, central locking provisions, and a center stand.

The new BMW 3 Series proves the sports sedan isn't dead yet, Lifestyle News
sum: After spending some time in Marseille, France, I start to wonder whether cars like the G50 BMW 3 Series M350 xDrive still have a place in a world obsessed with SUVs, batteries and increasingly absurd horsepower figures.
Here, the Mediterranean glistens in the distance as dramatically winding roads stretch out ahead, populated by compact French cars with varying interpretations of lane discipline.
There's also enough rain to make you briefly forget that back home in Singapore, owning a car requires the financial planning normally associated with buying industrial machinery.
And yet, behind the wheel of the all-new BMW M350 xDrive, one thought keeps returning to me: "Thank goodness BMW still makes cars like this."
That may sound melodramatic, but you must consider where Singapore's automotive trade is heading.

SUVs are everywhere, electric cars are getting obscenely powerful and the traditional combustion-engined sports sedan increasingly looks like the gentleman stubbornly wearing a suit to a casual Friday.
The new BMW M350 is therefore something refreshingly old-fashioned wrapped inside something thoroughly modern.

sum: BMW is pressing ahead with the industrial build-out behind its "Neue Klasse" electric range, bringing new battery plants online ahead of schedule even as parts shortages, a margin downgrade and a large U.S. recall test its supply chain and investor confidence.

Production chief Raymond Wittmann told Automobilwoche that the new battery factories are starting up earlier than planned, and that the iX3 has already drawn well over 100,000 orders for 2026. He conceded there are risks in ramping up new plants and technologies simultaneously. The stock shed 1.1% in the prior session.

The battery expansion reached a milestone on 13 November, when the group opened its Woodruff assembly plant in South Carolina and began series production of Gen6 high-voltage batteries. Those packs are destined for fully electric models built at the nearby Spartanburg factory, among them the iX5, with Woodruff handling battery assembly while the vehicles roll off the line next door.

Cell supply is being locked in as well. On 9 November BMW closed additional agreements for Gen6 cells: Samsung SDI will deliver from Europe, while LG Energy Solution will supply from the U.S. from the end of the 2020s.

The manufacturing push comes against a weaker financial backdrop. On 4 November the company lowered its margin forecast for the automotive business, now projecting an EBIT margin of ?0.5% to +0.5% for 2026, down from the 1–3% previously targeted. Free cash flow in the Automobiles segment is still expected to exceed EUR 2.5 billion.

Output has already been disrupted. BMW confirmed on 10 November that short-notice parts bottlenecks had forced production adjustments at individual plants, with the Handelsblatt reporting that three sites were affected. According to the newspaper's 12 November report, shifts were cancelled at Regensburg, Leipzig and Oxford because of missing wiring harnesses, with the shortfalls traced to Russian strikes on Ukrainian plants belonging to supplier Kromberg & Schubert. The paper, citing industry circles, said the harnesses were the component at issue.
On the safety front, the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on Friday urged owners of roughly 721,000 BMW vehicles to park outdoors and away from buildings because of fire risk.

BMW Starts iX5 Production, Reportedly Tells Suppliers: Fewer EVs
sum: BMW is building about 70 electric iX5 SUVs daily in Spartanburg, South Carolina, Automotive News reported on November 17th. It is BMW’s first U.S.-built electric vehicle (EV), with deliveries planned for early 2027.
The outlet says suppliers were told to plan for 60,000 U.S.-built EVs in 2027, down from 100,000 before. BMW hasn’t published these forecasts itself.

BMW built 412,799 X models at Spartanburg in 2025, the seventh time the plant has produced more than 400,000 vehicles in a year, BMW said in June. About half were exported to almost 120 countries. The reported 70 iX5s daily will be a small part of the plant’s total production, which the Greenville News puts at 1,500 vehicles per day.

The supplier forecast of 60,000 U.S.-built EVs next year is down 40% from the 100,000 previously forecast. These are supplier forecasts, not guaranteed production figures, as BMWBlog noted. BMW also told suppliers to get ready for 175,000 EVs per year for 2028 and 2029, as Automotive News reported.

BMW’s $700 million Woodruff factory began producing battery packs on November 13th, BMW said. It is just 15 miles (24 km) from Spartanburg, as the Greenville News reported. Both facilities are part of BMW’s completed $1.7 billion South Carolina investment.

Woodruff assembles battery packs using cells made by outside suppliers. BMW’s Woodruff announcement does not identify the factory supplying those cells. BMW named AESC as a U.S. cell supplier in 2022, and AESC paused construction of its South Carolina cell plant in June 2025, as I reported in combination with BMW’s recent new deals for cell suppliers.

The iX5 60 xDrive starts at $79,800, or $81,250 including destination. BMW first estimated up to 435 miles of range using preliminary U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) testing procedures, as EVXL reported. BMW has since raised that estimate to 450 miles, BMWBlog reported in October, citing a BMW product manager. U.S. deliveries are planned for the first quarter of 2027.

sum: The fifth generation hit the assembly line in August at the Spartanburg factory in the United States of America, and it also has a long wheelbase sibling, the G78, which comes to life in China, at the Dadong facility in Shenyang, for the local market. The G65 is based on an updated version of the old model’s CLAR construction, so despite looking entirely new, it shares many traits with its predecessor, though you cannot see them at first glance.

If you are familiar with BMW’s Neue Klasse design language, then you know why the new-gen X5 looks the way it does. And here, we are talking about the design of the kidney grille, which some say is a joke, whereas others definitely like. The same goes for the new X-shaped headlights, and the aggressive design of the front bumper, with its large air intake in the middle, separated in half by a pair of vertical slats, and the vents flanking it on the outer edges, and on the outer parts of the bumper.

Did you think that the profile is not controversial at all? In that case, you clearly haven’t heard that instead of traditional door handles, or even flush-mounted ones, the new-gen BMW X5 has some winglets. As a result, the doors look cleaner overall, at least on the upper sections, because the lower parts are on the sharp-looking side of things, just like the side skirts. BMW’s newest offering in its entry-level motorcycle range shares its engine and steel tubular chassis housing the engine as a stressed member, similar to its other two 450s. Its 420cc twin-cylinder liquid-cooled mill continues to mete out 48hp at 8,750rpm and 43Nm at 6,750rpm. Other technical aspects such as the suspension, brakes and kerb weight are closer to its sport-naked sibling, the F 450 R, with sportbike-like design details such as winglets and a full fairing, of course.

The F 450 RR has 17-inch tyres at both ends, KYB-supplied 43mm USD fork and monoshock suspension units, with the latter offering rebound and preload adjustability as standard. The standard seat height is 790mm, and BMW offers two seat options: increase it to 810mm or drop it down to 775mm. Brakes are the same as those on the R: a 310mm front disc with a Brembo four-piston monobloc caliper and a Bybre 240mm rear disc. The base variant of the F 450 RR has a kerb weight of 177kg.

The F 450 RR is available in four variants: Base, Sport, M Sport and M Sport with Innovation Package. As standard, all four get the exact same rider aids as the R, which include dual-channel and lean-sensitive ABS, a 6.5-inch TFT display with smartphone connectivity and three ride modes (Rain, Road and Race). sum: BMW is placing two very different bets this week — one on artificial intelligence that could reshape global supply chains, another on a user-interface philosophy that runs against the grain of its German rivals. Neither, however, is moving the needle for investors who remain fixated on the automaker's sagging share price.

The Munich-based company's venture arm, BMW i Ventures, has joined forces with Bosch Ventures, Hitachi Ventures and Yamaha Motor Ventures to back Nauta, a startup building autonomous AI agents for international goods trading. The platform, which describes itself as an operational command center for supply chains, claims to already work with more than 8,000 suppliers across 60 countries. Nauta says that in under six months, its software has prevented $3 million in delay-related costs, caught a $300,000 invoicing discrepancy and avoided $1.5 million in inventory outages, all while cutting operational hours per employee by 37 percent. For BMW i Ventures, the investment fits a broader strategy of getting early exposure to technologies promising efficiency gains along the supply chain — a priority that has gained urgency amid persistent global trade disruptions.

In its core business, BMW is charting a course that sets it apart from the rest of the industry. While Volkswagen and Mercedes-Benz have been reintroducing physical buttons in response to customer complaints, BMW is doubling down on touchscreens and voice control.

Vikram Pawah, head of BMW Australia, argues that younger buyers — roughly those up to age 45 — are comfortable multitasking and navigate digital interfaces with ease. The upcoming iX3, built on the "Neue Klasse" platform, will largely do away with traditional buttons. BMW points to the 2001 launch of iDrive as evidence of its digital pedigree.

The stance gets complicated by regulatory headwinds in China, where physical controls for functions like turn signals and windshield wipers are set to become mandatory from July 2027. The sudden profit warning triggered violent market turbulence, described by analysts as a "wake-up call" for the entire auto industry.

According to an ad-hoc announcement released by BMW Group on the evening of June 16, the core drivers behind the downgrade stem from multiple macroeconomic headwinds. Geopolitical conflicts in the Middle East have pushed up global energy costs and dampened consumer confidence, while tariff factors imposed by various countries are expected to drag down the automotive EBIT margin by approximately 1.25 percentage points. Most critically, the ongoing price war in Asia, particularly in China, continues to compress per-vehicle profitability. Group CEO Milan Nedeljkovic, newly appointed to the role, stated that the company must accelerate structural and efficiency measures to address the "dramatically deteriorating market environment."

Hit by this negative news, BMW shares on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange plunged more than 11% intraday on June 17, ultimately closing down 6.66%. Additionally, shares of OEMs and parts suppliers such as Forvia, Valeo, Renault, and Stellantis also fell in tandem.

Conversion of Preferred Shares into Ordinary Shares: BMW Group Simplifies Capital Structure
sum: Munich. BMW AG is simplifying its capital structure: its share capital of approximately €616 million will in future consist solely of ordinary shares. At today’s Annual General Meeting of BMW AG and a subsequently held separate meeting of preferred shareholders, the conversion of preferred shares into ordinary shares was approved by a clear majority. Approval at the Annual General Meeting amounted to 99,99%, while the separate meeting of preferred shareholders approved the resolution with 99,77%. The conversion will be brought into effect by way of an amendment to the Articles of Association, with no additional payment obligation for preferred shareholders. The conversion will become effective upon registration of the amendment to the Articles of Association in the commercial register. The BMW AG will announce the exact timing by public notice.

Currently, approximately 91% of BMW AG’s share capital consists of voting ordinary shares, and around 9% of non-voting preferred shares, which carry a fixed dividend preference of €0.02 per share. The dividend preference of the preferred shares will be applied for the last time for the 2025 financial year. From the 2026 financial year onward, the balance sheet profit available for distribution will be allocated evenly across all shares. Following the approved conversion at a ratio of 1:1,each share will in future carry the same voting right at the Annual General Meeting.

“For the weighting of BMW AG in major stock indices such as the DAX or the EURO STOXX 50, it is already the ordinary shares that are decisive as the share class with the highest free‑float market capitalization. As a result of the conversion, their proportion in free float will increase significantly by around 19%,” said Chief Financial Officer Walter Mertl on Wednesday in Munich. “This step therefore strengthens the weighting of BMW AG in relevant indices. The simplified capital structure represents a clear added value for investors and may have a positive impact on the share price performance of the BMW share.”

A single share structure follows the internationally recognised corporate governance principle of “one share, one vote”. This increases the attractiveness of the BMW share, in particular for international and institutional investors.

A German woman living between two very different worlds had South Africans laughing after she posted a video about something she noticed about how people live. She shared her thoughts on her TikTok page @ili_lebo on 4 March 2026, talking about how driving a German car, specifically a BMW, is seen in South Africa as a sign that you have truly made it in life. What amazed her was how different it was from back home, where the very people who build those cars are happily riding the train.

She explained that it goes deeper than just good public transport. In Germany and across much of Northern Europe, there is an unspoken social expectation that you should not stand out. She described it as looking very average on purpose. If you walk into a German mall wearing designer items and flashy jewellery, people do not admire you. Instead, you get what she called "the look". Which is a quiet mix of judgement and discomfort. Her South African boyfriend gave this mindset a name: the beige life.

This way of thinking actually has roots in a broader cultural concept found across Scandinavian and Northern European countries. The idea focuses on not thinking of yourself as better than anyone else, not showing off success and keeping things equal and modest across society. sum: - The 2027 BMW i3 is a new mid-size electric sedan that shares a newly developed architecture with the BMW iX3 SUV.

- The i3 is set to go on sale later this year, though BMW hasn't yet released pricing.

BMW's "Neue Klasse" mid-size cars of the 1960s saved the company. Now, BMW is using that term again, this time for a new generation of electric vehicles: the iX3 SUV and the i3 mid-size sedan. Their mission isn't quite as critical as their predecessors', but there's still a lot riding on this latest new class of cars.

The i3 is a nameplate we've seen before—on another pioneering model, a quirky city car offered as a pure EV or with an optional range extender. The new one is unrelated to the previous model. Instead, the model designation identifies it as the EV counterpart to the 3-series sedan, in the same way the i5 is analogous to the 5-series and the i7 to the 7-series. Compared with the current 3-series, the i3 is 1.6 inches longer overall, 1.5 inches wider, and 1.6 inches taller. It sits astride a wheelbase that has grown by nearly 2 inches.

Whereas the i5 and the i7 use the same platform as their gas-engine counterparts, the i3 uses a new platform unrelated to the 3-series. This one, used also by the iX3, features an 800-volt electrical architecture that's capable of ingesting juice at up to 400 kW (should we someday have public chargers that powerful). An NACS port is standard, with CCS compatibility via an adapter. The top AC charger in the U.S. will be a 15.4-kW unit. Its battery pack, which is a structural element in the car, has cells that are 20 percent more energy dense than those in the bigger BMW EVs; total battery capacity is 109 kWh. BMW estimates a maximum range of around 440 miles based on the EPA's testing procedure.

In the i3 50 xDrive model, those cells feed two motors that produce 463 horsepower and 476 pound-feet of torque (output for other i3 models hasn't yet been revealed). The computing power behind the i3 is new as well, consisting of four supercomputers, each controlling a group of functions.

Following its much maligned design direction of recent times, BMW has decided to tone things down a bit. Save for the new/old beaver toothed grille graphic, it’s a welcome departure from what’s gone before. From the front, a conventional ICE-looking lower bumper air intake area appears overly busy for an EV vehicle’s reduced cooling needs.

The new classically proportioned and illuminated kidneys are daintily styled, but too pinched, almost puckered up. The headlamps cleverly create a new lighting signature for the Neue Klasse, the angel eyes now replaced with snake eye graphics.

From the side, large wheels offset the blocky side volume, helping to give an impression of stability. Angled fender creases around the wheel openings are really the only design features in side view that inject any sense of surface entertainment. And yet, they’re a bit visually jarring and don’t quite work with the otherwise subdued side view.

Beyond that, smoothly surfaced body sides and an absence of protruding doorhandles contribute to a very low and respectable 0.24 drag coefficient – great for performance, not so good for visual fanfare.

At the rear, the iX3 has a well planted stance, albeit a bit generic. Long gone are the memorable days of BMW’s signature L-shaped taillights, replaced here with two horizontally positioned units, proudly providing a recessed area for the badge – a similar solution to the bonnet. The registration plate floats below the tailgate within a larger depressed area than needed. This solution stops the flow of the neighbouring surfaces, creating a harshly chiselled zone instead of a smoothly blended in form language.

items.t: Mercedes-Benz India Declines 2.85% In 2025 As BMW Gains Market Share, Highlighting Strategic Shift
sum: After five years of uninterrupted growth, Mercedes-Benz India reported a 2.85 percent year-on-year decline in retail sales in calendar year 2025, delivering 19,007 units compared with 19,565 units in 2024. The contraction marks the company’s first annual volume decline since 2020 and signals that its strategy of prioritising ‘value over volume’ may be eroding its grip on the entry and core luxury segments.

While Mercedes-Benz continues to tout record revenue, driven by high-margin top-end vehicles (TEVs), AMG models, and electric vehicles (EVs), the stark drop in entry-level sales exposes a vulnerability that rivals are increasingly exploiting.

The decline was largely concentrated in the entry luxury portfolio, which fell 20 per cent year-on-year, accounting for only 13 per cent of total volumes. Models such as the A-Class, GLA, and base C-Class variants have struggled to attract first-time luxury buyers, largely due to steep price increases and the absence of aggressive discounting, a deliberate strategy by the German carmaker to protect brand equity.

Meanwhile, the core segment contributed 62 per cent of total sales, and top-end vehicles accounted for 25 per cent. While these figures may sound healthy, the data highlights a skewed portfolio that relies heavily on premium and niche buyers, leaving Mercedes exposed in the high-volume, competitive mid-luxury segment.

Mercedes-Benz’s top-end vehicles, including the S-Class, Mercedes-Maybach, and AMG portfolio, posted 11 per cent growth, with AMG alone surging 34 per cent year-on-year. The EV portfolio grew 12 per cent, and BEVs accounted for 20 per cent of top-end sales, reflecting a clear emphasis on high-ticket products.

However, while these gains support revenue, they cannot compensate for volume losses in the entry segment, where aspirational buyers are increasingly gravitating toward rivals offering better pricing, financing, and newer EV options.

The competitive threat from BMW India is now undeniable. In CY2025, BMW Group India sold a record 18,001 cars, including 17,271 BMW units and 730 MINI cars, representing a 14 per cent year-on-year growth.

Apart from the myriad health concerns that come from vaping, vapes themselves can harm the environment in many ways.

When they're spent, vapes often become litter. Instead of disposing of them properly, people sometimes leave them along trails or in parks. Vapes left on the sides of roads can cause flat tires, leading to much frustration and stress for drivers.
